caption:
Epic Games has delayed its Marvel and Star Wars shooter and told developers to go "AI first" with tools like Anthropic's Claude, Bloomberg reports.
One director wrote: "No more hand-written code." CEO Tim Sweeney calls it a huge pivot for the company.

Would you play a game built mostly with AI?

Follow @neurafeed.ai for daily AI news.

Source: Bloomberg via Dexerto · Photos: Epic Games

slides.headline: Fortnite maker Epic Games just went AI first: *no more hand-written code*

image.generate: Inside a dim modern video game studio at night. A sleek white humanoid robot with a coral-orange asterisk-shaped light on its chest, the same coral orange as the asterisk logo in the first image, sits at the main workstation typing fast on a keyboard. Behind it, three young game developers in hoodies stand with arms crossed, looking stunned. The monitors show colorful cartoon-style 3D game characters like the ones in the second image, slightly blurred. The left third of the frame is empty dark background. The robot and the developers fill the upper two thirds of a vertical frame, with headroom above their heads; the bottom third is a dark desk. Blank surfaces, no readable text or labels on any object, no logos, no watermarks. It must look like an unedited real photo from a news agency, not a painting, not digital art, no glow effects.

slides.heading: The *Marvel and Star Wars* game slips
paras: Epic has delayed its unannounced shooter starring Marvel and Star Wars characters, Bloomberg reports. It was planned for March, and no new date has been set.
Sources say Epic underestimated how many people and how much time the project needed.

paras.t: It was meant to kick off Disney's $1.5 billion partnership with Epic.

slides.heading: *Claude* writes the code now
paras: Developers were told to follow an "AI first" model, using tools like Anthropic's Claude to generate code and art while humans guide the work.
One director wrote in an internal message: "No more hand-written code." All artwork will be made with full AI workflows, according to the report.

slides.heading: Developers were *stunned*
paras: The news reportedly surprised staff on a video call in early October. Some asked how AI mistakes would be caught, and others doubted the plan would work.
Bloomberg says it is the first time a major game company has tried to build a title mainly with AI.

slides.heading: Tim Sweeney: *it's not 2016*
paras: Epic CEO Tim Sweeney confirmed a "huge pivot" on X, moving developers around to retool for maximum AI acceleration.
He said the goal is to build more, not to do the same work with fewer people. "Much of the room wants it to be 2016 again, but it's not," he wrote.

slides.hook: Follow to see if Epic's AI-built shooter actually ships, and what gamers think of it.
